newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Speculation in Dominican Republic over Fujimori visit.
newsitem.headline: Speculation in Dominican Republic over Fujimori visit.

text.p: Peru's embassy in the Dominican Republic on Wednesday denied media speculation that Peru's president asked the Dominican government to offer asylum to the Marxist rebels holding hostages in Lima.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori met with Dominican President Leonel Fernandez during a four-hour stopover in Santo Domingo on Tuesday. The two men spoke for about half an hour at an airport meeting room, but said little to the press when they emerged.

Local newspaper and television reports speculated that Fujimori made the extended stopover to ask Fernandez to take in the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas who seized more than 500 people during a party at the residence Dec. 17, 1996, and were still holding 72 hostages.
"The report that that subject was part of the conversation is false information," Peruvian ambassador Benjamin Ruiz told Reuters.
Ruiz sat in on the meeting between the two men and said they had discussed only the prospects for a visit to the Dominican Republic by Fujimori and unspecified "bilateral" issues.
"There was no such request, and I guarantee that strongly," he said.

When reporters spoke with him after the meeting, Fujimori offered no response when asked if he had raised the asylum issue. And Fernandez said only that Fujimori had expressed his desire to see more of the Dominican Republic.
Before the meeting, Fujimori had said he hoped to make a state visit to the Caribbean nation soon.
The daily newspaper Listin Diario on Wednesday ran a front-page report that Fujimori had made the asylum request.
